note: Frozen twin case table for pointer-scoped external reference composition and reference traversal. the openapi family specifications section 6 'Reference scope': a reference that leaves the current document composes the value at the referenced JSON Pointer together with that value's transitive closure of references, and nothing else. the openapi family specifications section 6 'Reference traversal': a $ref standing in a fragment's own path is resolved and evaluation continues into the target under OAS 3.0.0-3.0.4, and is not under OAS 3.1.0-3.1.2, where the reference is unresolvable. Each case is a multi-document artifact plus the one verdict every engine must reach; the two 'same-document-pointer-below-a-reference' cases are the exception, and carry one document, because the traversal rule is a property of a fragment and the document it is evaluated against rather than of the reference having left the document. The identical file is executed by openbindings-go's formats/openapi, by openapi-client/go, and by openbindings-ts's packages/openapi; a divergence in one fails the others' suites too. The sibling-kind cases vary the JSON kind of a sequence index nothing composes, at two positions, because section 6 and RFC 6901 draw no line there and an engine that reads the sequence with a typed model can. Every case is authored from the OAS, JSON Reference, JSON Schema 2020-12 and RFC 6901 text; no byte comes from a corpus specimen, and no case pins an implementations' convention. The traversal authorities are quoted per edition in each engine's own reference-traversal comment and re-derived at the pinned bytes by corpus-lab/scripts/verify-pointer-below-reference-authorities.mjs.

cases.name: defect-outside-the-composed-closure
cases.why: A dangling reference in a component the pointer never reaches is outside the composed closure, so the referencing artifact resolves (the openapi family specifications section 6).

https://composition.example/openapi.yaml.text:
openapi: 3.1.2
info: {title: Entry, version: "1"}
servers: [{url: "https://api.example"}]
paths:
  /items:
    post:
      operationId: createItem
      requestBody:
        required: true
        content:
          application/json:
            schema: {$ref: "./library.yaml#/components/schemas/Used"}
      responses: {"204": {description: ok}}

cases.name: defect-inside-the-composed-closure
cases.why: A reference reachable from the referenced pointer, and unresolvable there, does make the referencing artifact unresolvable.

cases.name: target-is-not-an-openapi-document

cases.name: pointer-into-a-bare-json-schema-file

cases.name: cycle-spanning-two-documents

cases.name: pointer-below-a-reference-3.0.0
cases.why: Reference traversal, FOLLOWING branch. Under OAS 3.0.0 a $ref is processed as per JSON Reference (section 4.6 'Relative References in URLs', and the Reference Object's 'The Reference Object is defined by JSON Reference and follows the same structure, behavior and rules' plus 'reference resolution is accomplished as defined by the JSON Reference specification and not by the JSON Schema specification'). JSON Reference states its own basis as transclusion (section 1), ignores every member other than $ref (section 3), and resolves to the referenced value (section 4). So a reference standing in this pointer's path is resolved and evaluation continues into the target. This is the incorporated authority's answer, not these implementations' convention.

cases.name: pointer-below-a-reference-3.1.0
cases.why: Reference traversal, REFUSING branch, at the SAME position as its pointer-below-a-reference-3.0.4 twin and with a byte-identical artifact apart from the declared edition. Under OAS 3.1.0 section 4.6 'Relative References in URIs', 'If the representation of the referenced document is JSON or YAML, then the fragment identifier SHOULD be interpreted as a JSON-Pointer as per [RFC6901]' — over the REFERENCED DOCUMENT — and the 3.1 Schema Object is a superset of JSON Schema 2020-12, whose section 8.2.3.1 makes $ref an applicator whose 'results are the results of the referenced schema', with the authors' note that other keywords may sit alongside it. Nothing is substituted, so the node keeps its one member, the next token identifies nothing, and RFC 6901 section 4's error condition arises. No 3.1 edition mentions JSON Reference at all.

cases.name: deep-pointer-with-no-reference-in-its-path-3.1.2
cases.why: Negative control for the refusing branch. The same depth of pointer, the same edition and the same library, but every node on the path is spelled out, so no token is ever looked up inside a $ref object and RFC 6901 section 4 resolves a concrete value for every token. cases.name: pointer-lands-on-a-reference-3.1.2

An engine that refused whenever a $ref appeared anywhere near a pointer would fail here.

cases.name: whole-file-reference-composes-the-file
cases.why: A reference with no fragment addresses the resource root, so the composed value is the whole file and a defect anywhere in it is inside the closure.

cases.name: defect-in-a-sibling-sequence-element
cases.why: A sequence member is addressed by index exactly as an object member is addressed by name: the composed value is allOf/0, so the defective allOf/1 beside it is outside the closure and the referencing artifact resolves.

cases.name: two-pointers-into-one-sequence
cases.why: Two references compose two elements of the same sequence, and the element between them - which nothing composes and which is defective - is outside the closure. allOf/2 must still denote the third element, so no index may be renumbered.

cases.name: sequence-sibling-is-a-string
cases.why: A string beside the composed element. Section 6 makes a defect outside the composed closure irrelevant 'however the referenced document is stored', and RFC 6901 section 4 addresses a sequence element by index exactly as it addresses an object member by name. Neither draws a line at the sibling's JSON kind, so this must resolve to the same operation and the same emitted schema as a mapping sibling.
